title: LLM-Augmented Cross-Stock Semantic Network for Lead-Lag Trading

source.paper: Cross-Stock Predictability via LLM-Augmented Semantic Networks
source.authors: Yikuan Huang, Zheqi Fan, Kaiqi Hu, Yifan Ye

hypothesis: A two-stage framework — sparse candidate graph from 10-K embeddings + LLM edge classification by economic link type (CUSTOMER_SUPPLIER / COMPETITOR / COMMON_INPUT) — generates durable stock linkages that predict cross-stock return lead-lag (1-week horizon) better than correlation-based peer networks. Asymmetric links (supplier → customer) capture lead-lag alpha; symmetric links (competitors) generate mean-reversion alpha. Test on top-100 S&P 500 stocks.
distinction_from_h316: H316 (Moira) uses LLM for pair selection then trades mean-reversion. H319 distinguishes link TYPE and routes to different strategies: asymmetric→lead-lag momentum, symmetric→pairs mean-reversion. Also uses 10-K filing embeddings (structured), not free-text company descriptions.

design.data: SEC EDGAR 10-K Item 1 (business description), fetched via EdgarTools
design.stage1: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small embeddings → cosine sim → top-10 candidates per stock
design.stage2: GPT-4o-mini classifies each candidate edge: CUSTOMER_SUPPLIER / COMPETITOR / COMMON_INPUT / NONE + link_direction for asymmetric
design.signal_asymmetric: When supplier stock returns positive in week t, trade customer stock long in week t+1
design.signal_symmetric: Rolling 20d z-score on spread; entry ±1.5σ, exit 0.3σ
design.gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.0 AND Corr-SPY < 0.40 AND WF 0.5-4.0

estimated_cost: $5-15 for 10-K download + LLM scoring of ~500 candidate pairs on 100-stock universe; monthly rescoring <$1
